questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F={x}^{2}yz\,i+{x}^{3}y\,j+z\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})\,k.$ Evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-1,-1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})) \\  & =2xyz+{x}^{3}+\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-1,-1,2),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F(-1,-1,2) & =2(-1)(-1)(2)+(-1)^{3}+\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-1}{-1}) \\  & =4-1+\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =3+\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14159207/assets/2b64c156519b685acf390c51c1ea3e1540d82e0f7e047cf2f804d38a23956604.png)

Consider the vector field $F$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true everywhere in the domain of $F?$

I. $∇\cdot F=0$

II. $∇\cdot F>0$

III. $∇\cdot F<0$

IV. $F$ is solenoidal
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F$ denotes the divergence of the vector field $F.$

Intuitively, the divergence of $F$ at a point $P$ measures how much $F$ acts like a source or a sink at $P:$

- If $F$ acts like a source at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F>0$ at $P.$

- If $F$ acts like a sink at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F<0$ at $P.$

- If $F$ acts like neither a source nor a sink at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F=0$ at $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14159207/assets/6c747149618d4c5ef35e727af15cd001365bd9c2d5e064689baf24c6ee23cff9.png)

If $∇\cdot F=0$ everywhere in the domain of $F,$ we say that $F$ is solenoidal.

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement II is true, whereas statements I and III are false. Notice that the length of the vectors' $x$-components increase as we move away from the origin in the horizontal direction. Therefore, the vector field $F$ acts like a source at every point.

- Statement IV is false. Since $∇\cdot F\ne 0,$ the vector field $F$ is not solenoidal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem: Consider the vector field $F=(x-y)^{3}\,i+(y+z)^{3}\,j+(x+z)^{3}\,k.$ Evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-2,2,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-y)^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂y}((y+z)^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂z}((x+z)^{3}) \\  & =3(x-y)^{2}+3(y+z)^{2}+3(x+z)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-2,2,2),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F(-2,2,2) & =3((-2)-(2))^{2}+3((2)+(2))^{2}+3((-2)+(2))^{2} \\  & =3(-4)^{2}+3(4)^{2}+3(0)^{2} \\  & =96.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy{z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{z}^{3}) \\  & =2y{z}^{2}+x{e}^{y}+3y{z}^{2} \\  & =5y{z}^{2}+x{e}^{y}.\end{aligned}
$$
